holidays.name: National Bean Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the humble legume, from baked beans to black beans to jelly beans if you're feeling cheeky. Chili pots, burrito bars, and cassoulet everywhere get their moment in the spotlight.
holidays.origin: An informal American food observance that grew out of food-calendar lists, celebrating beans as an inexpensive, nutritious staple that has fed people for thousands of years.
holidays.funFact: Beans are among the oldest cultivated crops in the world, with evidence of cultivation dating back thousands of years, and the Romans reportedly used beans as voting tokens.

holidays.name: Epiphany / Three Kings' Day (with King Cake Season Kickoff)
holidays.description: A Christian feast marking the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus, celebrated with parades, gifts, and elaborate cakes. In many places it kicks off a season of hiding tiny trinkets in pastries and crowning whoever finds them.
holidays.origin: Observed since the early centuries of Christianity. Traditions like the Rosca de Reyes in Mexico, Roscón in Spain, and King Cake in New Orleans (where Mardi Gras season begins) developed from medieval European customs.
holidays.funFact: In New Orleans, whoever finds the plastic baby in their slice of King Cake is traditionally expected to buy the next cake or host the next party.

holidays.name: Cuddle Up Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to snuggling under blankets with loved ones, pets, or a strategically heated pile of pillows. Perfect for the dead of winter when leaving the couch seems like a poor life choice.
holidays.origin: An unofficial wintertime observance, popularized through social media and holiday calendars, that encourages warmth and closeness during the coldest part of the year.
holidays.funFact: Cuddling is associated with the release of oxytocin, often nicknamed the 'bonding hormone,' which can help lower stress.

holidays.name: Old Christmas (Armenian Christmas)
holidays.description: Several Eastern Orthodox and Apostolic traditions celebrate Christmas on January 6 or 7 instead of December 25, complete with fasting, special services, and a hearty feast afterward.
holidays.origin: Armenian Apostolic Christians have long observed the Nativity together with Epiphany on January 6, a practice that predates the separate December 25 Christmas date adopted in the Western church.
holidays.funFact: Armenia is one of the few places where Christmas and Epiphany are celebrated on the same day, with a traditional dish of fish, rice, and nevik (spinach-based) dishes after the fast.

holidays.name: Sherlock Holmes' Birthday (Unofficial Fan Celebration)
holidays.description: Mystery fans toast the world's most famous consulting detective with deerstalker hats, violin serenades, and dramatic pipe-free pondering. Bonus points for deducing who ate the last biscuit.
holidays.origin: Members of the Baker Street Irregulars, a Sherlockian society founded in 1934, celebrate the fictional detective's birthday around this date, with a traditional January 6 birthday often cited by fans based on Holmes scholarship.
holidays.funFact: Sherlock Holmes never actually says 'Elementary, my dear Watson' in any of Arthur Conan Doyle's original stories.
